model_organism.citation: Nuclear export inhibitors avert progression in preclinical models of inflammatory demyelination (PMID: 25706475)
model_organism.organism: mouse (cultured neurons; in vivo work used pharmacological CRM1 inhibitors, not genetic knockout)
phenotypes: Xpo1 knockdown in cultured neurons was neuroprotective, mirroring the effect of pharmacological CRM1 inhibition
Pharmacological CRM1 inhibitors attenuated disease progression in murine demyelination models, including when started after onset of paralysis
CRM1 inhibitors decreased immune cell proliferation, with nuclear accumulation of cell cycle inhibitors
CRM1 inhibitors preserved cytoskeletal integrity in demyelinated axons
CRM1 inhibitors were neuroprotective in the kainic acid model of axonal damage
In neurons, CRM1 inhibitors prevented nuclear export of molecules associated with axonal damage and retained neuroprotective transcription factors

biological.citation: Pathogenic XPO1 variants cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 40819229)
biological.summary: Ubiquitous and neuron-specific XPO1 knockdown in Drosophila impaired development. GABAergic neuron-specific knockdown impaired habituation learning. De novo XPO1 variants (half putative LoF, half missense or in-frame deletion) in 22 individuals define a dominant monogenic neurodevelopmental disorder.
biological.sample_size: 22 individuals with de novo XPO1 variants

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Functional characterization of the 2p15-16 microdeletion
biological.summary: XPO1 RNAi knockdown in C. elegans causes early embryonic lethality. An XPO1::GFP transgene is expressed ubiquitously throughout development and in adults. XPO1 lies in the minimal deleted region of the 2p15-16 microdeletion.

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Functional characterization of the 2p15-16 microdeletion
biological.summary: XPO1 is expressed in adult mouse brain, gut and lung. In human fetal brain it shows mild positivity in immature ependyma and Cajal-Retzius cells. Whole-genome expression showed no copy-number-related reduction of XPO1 in patient samples.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Driver genes for 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome identified using clinical, genomic and functional analysis
biological.summary: XPO1 is dosage sensitive, with reduced protein in patient lymphoblast lines. XPO1 deletion co-segregated with nuclear accumulation of the export cargo rpS5. Zebrafish xpo1a knockdown caused microcephaly, dysmorphic body, growth defects and brain abnormalities, implicating XPO1 as a driver gene.

biological.citation: Exportin-1 functions as an adaptor for transcription factor-mediated docking of chromatin at the nuclear pore complex (PMID: 40068679)
biological.summary: In yeast, Crm1/Xpo1 binds Gcn4 and Nup2 directly and co-occupies enhancers with Nups. Crm1 inhibition blocks Nup2-genome interaction. The Crm1-Gcn4 interaction needs neither Ran-GTP nor the NES-binding site, and Crm1/Ran-GTP stimulate Gcn4 DNA binding.

biological.citation: Nuclear export of R-loop by the DDX1 and XPO1 complex promotes senescence-associated secretory phenotype and inflammaging (PMID: 42303864)
biological.summary: An XPO1-DDX1 complex is essential for nuclear export of R-loops into cytoplasmic chromatin fragments in senescent cells, activating cGAS-STING and the SASP. XPO1 inhibition with KPT-330 blocked R-loop export, attenuated the SASP and inflammation, and extended healthspan.

XPO1 deletion in DEK::NUP214 FKH-1 cells showed strong dependency. XPO1 co-localizes with DEK::NUP214 at chromatin, and eltanexor disrupted this, down-regulating cell-cycle and self-renewal targets. Eltanexor delayed leukemia in a PDX model (median 377 vs 244 days).

biological.citation: Impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport in SOD1-mediated ALS (PMID: 41691309)
biological.summary: Mutant SOD1 disrupts nuclear import and export and causes cytosolic accumulation of XPO1 and RanGAP1. AAV-mediated reduction of mutant SOD1 restored nuclear XPO1 localization in transgenic mice. Similar changes appeared in patient fibroblasts and postmortem spinal cord.

biological.citation: Function of Nup98 subtypes and their fusion proteins, Nup98-TopIIβ and Nup98-SETBP1 in nuclear-cytoplasmic transport (PMID: 28392395)
biological.summary: Nup98-TopIIβ and Nup98-SETBP1 partially co-localize with XPO1 and full-length Nup98, and negatively regulate XPO1-mediated protein export.

biological.citation: Mutant NPM1 Maintains the Leukemic State through HOX Expression (PMID: 30205049)
biological.summary: XPO1 mediates cytoplasmic export of mutant NPM1c. XPO1 inhibition relocalizes NPM1c to the nucleus, down-regulates HOX genes, promotes differentiation of AML cells and prolongs survival of Npm1-mutated leukemic mice.

biological.citation: Exportin 1 (XPO1) Expression and Effectiveness of XPO1 Inhibitor Against Canine Lymphoma Cell Lines (PMID: 40872651)
biological.summary: XPO1 mRNA and protein are highly expressed in 17-71, CLBL-1, CLC, CLGL-90 and UL-1 canine lymphoma lines, and moderately in GL-1, Ema and Nody-1. KPT-335 inhibited growth in all lines (IC50 89.8-418 nM), with no correlation between XPO1 level and drug efficacy.
